question: Should OpenClaw sponsor official FreeBSD support, and if so should it be documented as community/experimental support or promoted toward Tier 1 release support?
rationale: Current main does not provide the official support contract, but a FreeBSD ports package exists externally, so the remaining choice is support tier, ownership, and whether OpenClaw wants to validate or advertise that platform.

options.title: Define community FreeBSD scope first
options.body: Recognize the external ports/pkg path only as community or experimental until owners, docs, service behavior, upgrade tracking, and release-smoke expectations are named.

options.title: Promote FreeBSD toward Tier 1
options.body: Accept ongoing FreeBSD release ownership and open tracked implementation work for pkg/ports coordination, service management, CI, docs, and validation.

options.title: Decline official FreeBSD support
options.body: Leave FreeBSD as external/community packaging and close this support-tier request after documenting the policy.

recommendation.title: Define community FreeBSD scope first
recommendation.body: Recognize the external ports/pkg path only as community or experimental until owners, docs, service behavior, upgrade tracking, and release-smoke expectations are named.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses official support scope, installer publication, release validation, and project roadmap ownership.
